title: Invest in Gold Digitally: Understanding NSE Electronic Gold Receipts
description: Electronic Gold Receipts (EGRs) allow investors to own gold in a dematerialised form, similar to shares. Traded on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), each EGR.

faq.q: What is an Electronic Gold Receipt (EGR)?
faq.a: An EGR is a digital instrument representing ownership of physical gold of a specified purity and quantity, typically 1 gram of 995 purity gold, stored in SEBI-approved vaults. It is traded on stock exchanges like the NSE.

Electronic Gold Receipts are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). SEBI oversees the exchanges, vaulting agencies, and other intermediaries involved to ensure investor protection and market integrity.

faq.q: Can I convert my EGRs into physical gold?
faq.a: Yes, one of the key features of EGRs is their convertibility into physical gold. Investors holding a minimum specified quantity (e.g., 10 grams) can request their broker to convert their electronic units into physical gold, which is then delivered from the vault.

EGRs are considered safe as they are backed by physical gold stored in SEBI-regulated vaults, ensuring purity and security. The trading platform is regulated by SEBI, providing transparency and investor safeguards.

faq.q: How are capital gains on EGRs taxed?
faq.a: Short-term capital gains (holding period up to 36 months) are added to your income and taxed at your slab rate. Long-term capital gains (holding period over 36 months) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment required for EGRs?
faq.a: EGRs are typically traded in units of 1 gram, making them accessible even for small investments. The minimum investment would be the price of one gram of gold plus brokerage and GST.

faq.q: How do EGRs differ from Gold ETFs?
faq.a: While both are digital ways to invest in gold, EGRs represent direct ownership of physical gold in a vault with an option for physical conversion. Gold ETFs are units of a mutual fund that invests in physical gold, offering indirect exposure to gold prices.
